title: The football field
objectives: Answer out loud: What's a football field and how is it used?

steps.body: A horizontal bar chart: each bar shows the low–high per-share value from one method.
Usually includes the 52-week trading range for context.
Bankers use it to frame a price range for a sale, a fairness opinion, or a pitch.

blocks.template: A football field shows {{1}}, not single values
The 52-week range is a {{1}}, not a valuation method

blocks.title: Why show ranges instead of a single number?
blocks.body:
Every method depends on assumptions. Showing ranges is honest about uncertainty and shows where methods overlap — the overlap is often where the negotiated price lands.

**Interview answer:** "Every method has uncertainty, so ranges are more honest, and the overlap between methods shows the defensible price."

blocks.title: Why include the 52-week trading range?
blocks.teaser: It shows where the market has actually valued the stock.
blocks.body: It shows where the market has actually valued the stock. A buyer offering below the 52-week low would struggle to get shareholder approval.

blocks.prompt: Why include the 52-week trading range on a football field?

options.text: It's the most reliable valuation method
It shows where the market has actually valued the stock — a reference point
It replaces the DCF for public companies
Regulators require it in every pitch

blocks.explanation: It's a reference point, not a valuation method — an offer below the 52-week low would struggle to win shareholder approval.
